correctness.rationale: The repair explicitly assumes n>0 for the strict universal inequality and corrects attribution of the mark model. In the repaired proof I checked the nonadjacent conditional integral by splitting at y=z, and the adjacent integral by the beta integral on the excluded triangle y+z≤1. At d=2 the one-common-neighbor joint probability is 2/15 and the adjacent one is 5/24; subtracting 1/9 gives 1/45 and 7/72. Ordered codegree sum is nd(d−1); individual variance cancels the subtraction across ordered edges. For a nonzero codegree the sharp summand bound is attained iff t=d, so any two neighbors of a vertex are false twins; their common neighborhoods create degree-saturated K_{d,d} components. The d=1 endpoint gives R_1=1 and matchings. The exact coefficient deficit is positive after the central-binomial correction and vanishes as d grows, with equality hosts certifying optimality of the limit constant. Read the frozen script and verification note; the recorded 125 comparisons are finite corroboration, not used for the general proof. The complete repaired RESULT.md has the corrected assumptions, proof and attribution.

value.rationale: Isolation is a canonical degree-count statistic in the dependent threshold model. The exact finite-degree coefficient sharply improves the published all-degree variance scale on this class, distinguishes the role of codegrees from shared edges, and identifies degree-saturated extremizers. The result can be used as a sharp second-moment benchmark without making unsupported high-probability or other-degree claims.
